question: Define the term velocity factor. Why is it relevant to communications networks?
answer: "Velocity factor is the ratio of the speed at which a signal moves through a communications medium relative to the speed of light. Velocity factors are important in networking because they determine the propagation delay
rubric: and therefore ultimately influences how fast a message can be received.. A medium with a high velocity factor transmits data near the speed of light
